inputs.source: Nightly batch of CRM account rows

instructions.note: The prompt requires completion of every row and says to keep going until every row is complete, with no bounded retry or stop condition.

elements.name: Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota

controls.name: Maximum unattended step and retry limit
Hard spend cap or quota partition for enrichment calls
Sub-agent spawn depth and concurrency limit

findings.title: Spend loop (TC6): unbounded retries and recursive sub-agents can exhaust the shared enrichment quota

forecast.watch_signal: Nightly row count, median retries per row, and spawned sub-agent count rise; new data sources or broader use of the shared enrichment quota are added.

evidence.observation: The agent is instructed to use enrich.lookup for each row, retry incomplete lookups, spawn a researcher sub agent when needed, and keep going until every row is complete.
There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents, and sub agents can spawn their own researchers.
enrich.lookup is billed per call and uses an API key and monthly quota shared with sales and marketing; if the quota runs out, their tools stop working until the next month.
The nightly batch is 40,000 rows and about 3 percent have malformed company names that never return a complete result, creating a persistent retry condition.
There is no spend alert on the enrichment account.

recommendations.action: Enforce hard limits on retries, unattended steps, runtime, sub-agent depth, and total API calls per batch so malformed rows terminate instead of looping.
Apply a hard spend cap or partition the monthly enrichment quota so this agent cannot consume the quota needed by sales and marketing.
Add spend and anomaly alerts on retry rate, lookup volume, and spawned sub-agent count so runaway jobs are detected before the shared quota is exhausted.

stride_coverage.rationale: The provided artifacts describe no inbound authentication surface, peer identity claim, or impersonable protocol endpoint for this agent.
The design states the agent cannot modify its own configuration, and no writable prompt, tool definition, or memory store is described.
The artifacts do not describe logging, action provenance, or whether API calls and CRM writes are attributable to this agent.
No egress of sensitive data is described beyond paid lookup requests for enrichment, and this assessment has no evidence of disclosure risk.
Credential scope for spawned sub-agents is not described well enough to determine whether delegated actions exceed the principal's authority.
The nightly batch source is an internal scheduled feed, and the artifacts provide no identity mechanism or spoofing exposure to evaluate.
The artifacts do not say whether row provenance is preserved from CRM through enrichment processing.
The artifacts do not describe quota governance, write protections, or who can alter the shared API key and monthly quota settings.
The artifacts mention a shared API key but do not describe storage protections, secret exposure paths, or access controls on the key material.
The design does not state whether the outbound enrichment API flow has integrity protections or request validation controls.
The artifacts do not say what account data is sent to the enrichment service or whether the transport and payload logging are protected.

rating.rationale: Present risk is driven by a property finding: an A4 autonomous nightly enrichment design with no limits on retries, runtime, steps, or recursive sub-agents, calling a paid shared-quota API over a 40,000-row batch where about 3 percent of rows never complete. Under rubric section 5a, the affected capability set includes S3 spend and delegate actions, giving an I-row base of high; the autonomy modifier applies but the property-finding cap keeps inherent at high. No declared or verified preventive controls restore spend, step, runtime, or delegation limits, so residual remains high. Forecast remains high because there are no present controls to decay; the watch items are growth in batch size, retries, spawned researchers, or broader quota scope. Manual validation applied from validation_checklist.md; no runtime behavior was observed.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No runtime configuration, orchestration policy, telemetry, or billing guardrail implementation artifacts were provided, so control absence is assessed from the notes and confidence is limited to declared design evidence.

No protocol, credential storage, or logging details were provided, so STRIDE coverage for spoofing, repudiation, information disclosure, and elevation of privilege is partly not_assessed rather than fully rated.
